methodological_rigor.justification: This study combines correlative human evidence (TCGA survival stratified by an optimized LGALS1 cutoff and IHC in paired OSCC/normal tissues, n = 73) with mechanistic in vitro assays and a xenograft model to test whether Triptolide (TPL) induces ferroptosis via Galectin-1 modulation (Methods 2.1–2.13; Results 3.1–3.6). The functional claims are supported by dose/time viability assays, lipid ROS increases with partial rescue by Ferrostatin-1, and GPX4 downregulation, plus Gal-1 knockdown/restoration experiments (Results 3.2–3.5). However, ferroptosis inference relies mainly on lipid ROS and GPX4 changes, with limited orthogonal biochemical/genetic validation and most mechanistic work concentrated in one main cell line (SAS), which the Discussion acknowledges as a limitation (Discussion; Conclusions). The statistical approach is standard (t-tests/chi-square/log-rank) but largely unadjusted and does not address multiplicity across many readouts.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is primarily preclinical (cell lines and xenograft) with supporting correlative human tissue and TCGA associations, so Oxford LoE is best classified as 5 for therapeutic inference (Methods 2; Results 3). Clinical relevance is direct because OSCC has limited effective options in advanced disease and the paper links high Galectin-1 to worse overall survival and advanced stage while proposing a druggable ferroptosis-sensitization axis (Results 3.1; Conclusions). The translational path remains uncertain because efficacy is shown only in xenografts and mechanistic hierarchy (e.g., NRF2 axis) is described as hypothetical and needing targeted validation (Discussion).

reporting_quality.justification: Because this manuscript mixes cohort survival analysis, human IHC, cell biology assays, and mouse xenografts, no single reporting checklist (e.g., STROBE/ARRIVE) is explicitly applied in the normalized text, so 'other' is most appropriate (Methods 2). The methods describe key experimental components (cell lines, dosing, lipid ROS probe, GPX4 WB, xenograft and IHC scoring) and define clinical endpoints for tissue associations, which supports interpretability (Methods 2.2–2.12). Data/code sharing is not described beyond use of public TCGA resources and standard software, so reproducibility of the wet-lab results and analysis scripts appears limited in the provided manuscript.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is the specific linkage of Galectin-1 suppression to ferroptosis-associated vulnerability in OSCC and the framing of TPL as a Gal-1-modulating ferroptosis sensitizer supported by human expression/prognosis associations (Abstract; Results 3.1–3.5). TPL’s anticancer effects and ferroptosis induction by diverse compounds are established themes, so the contribution is more a context-specific mechanistic extension than a new paradigm (Introduction; Discussion). The manuscript itself emphasizes that parts of the pathway model (e.g., NRF2 involvement) remain to be validated, which limits how far novelty can be claimed (Discussion).

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract clearly states the OSCC problem, the hypothesized Gal-1/ferroptosis mechanism, the experimental components (TCGA, IHC, cell lines, xenograft), and the main direction of effects (lipid ROS up, GPX4 down, Gal-1 down) (Abstract). Methods are well segmented and sufficiently detailed for core assays (IHC scoring rubric, drug dosing range, lipid ROS detection, and xenograft workflow) (Methods 2.2–2.13). The Discussion appropriately qualifies causal claims and lists concrete limitations (marker scope for ferroptosis; cell-line breadth), improving transparency (Discussion; Conclusions).

key_strengths: Multi-layer evidence combining TCGA survival association, paired-tissue IHC (n = 73), in vitro assays, and xenograft readouts around a consistent Gal-1/ferroptosis narrative.
Functional experiments include ferroptosis inhibitor rescue (Ferrostatin-1) and Galectin-1 knockdown/restoration elements rather than relying on expression correlations alone.
Clear clinical framing: high Galectin-1 associates with poorer OS and advanced stage, positioning the pathway as potentially biomarker-relevant in OSCC (Results 3.1).
key_concerns: Ferroptosis is inferred primarily from lipid ROS and GPX4 changes; stronger orthogonal validation (e.g., iron chelation/lipid peroxidation chemistry panels or genetic GPX4 rescue) is not shown and is acknowledged as a limitation.
Most mechanistic depth is concentrated in SAS cells, limiting generalizability across OSCC models and patient-derived systems (Discussion).
Reproducibility posture is weak in the normalized manuscript (no explicit data/code release or detailed analytic scripts for the bioinformatics component).
chief_reviewer.rationale: The paper presents a plausible, clinically motivated ferroptosis-sensitization mechanism with supportive human associations and in vivo xenograft evidence, but the mechanistic and validation depth is not yet sufficient for a higher tier; with major revisions focused on ferroptosis specificity and broader model validation, it fits a tier-3 oncology venue.
